# Communication Preferences

<!-- observed: 2026-07-27 | status: active -->
- **Goes by:** **Diane** (never "Ms. Castellano," never the full "Diane Castellano" in greetings).
<!-- observed: 2026-07-27 | status: active -->
- **Tone:** warm but efficient; lead with the recommendation and the operational or
  patient-safety impact.
<!-- observed: 2026-07-27 | status: active -->
- **Plain language:** Diane is **not technical** — explain Epic/IT and clinical-systems issues
  in operational terms, not jargon or acronyms she hasn't adopted. Spell out an acronym the
  first time.
<!-- observed: 2026-07-27 | status: active -->
- **Format:** short written pre-reads with clear owners and dates; bullets over prose.
<!-- observed: 2026-07-27 | status: active -->
- **Escalation:** flag anything that could surprise Marcus (CEO) or the board **before** it
  reaches them — especially quality, accreditation, and Epic issues.
<!-- observed: 2026-07-27 | status: active -->
- **Channels:** internal messaging for quick items; email for anything to an external party
  (payer, accreditor); formal document for board and regulator materials.
